scenes.heading: Percentage of a quantity
scenes.say: Thirty per cent off! Ten per cent tip! Percentages are everywhere when you shop. Today you'll learn how to work out exactly how many dollars a percentage stands for.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Spread $200 over 100 equal squares: each square is $2
scenes.breaks: Real things don't always split into 100 neat pieces, like 15% of 7 people.
scenes.say: Picture any amount spread evenly over one hundred squares. One square is one per cent. Spread two hundred dollars over one hundred squares and each one is worth two dollars. So fifteen per cent is fifteen squares: thirty dollars.
scenes.caption: Picture any amount spread evenly over 100 squares. One square is 1%. Spread $200 over 100 squares and each is worth $2. So 15% is 15 squares: $30.

scenes.heading: "Of" means multiply
scenes.say: Just like with fractions, of means multiply. Thirty per cent of two hundred and fifty is zero point three times two hundred and fifty, which is seventy-five. You can use a fraction or a decimal.
scenes.caption: Just like with fractions, "of" means multiply. 30% of 250 = 0.3 × 250 = 75. You can use a fraction or a decimal.

scenes.heading: Mental building blocks
scenes.say: In your head, use building blocks. Ten per cent: divide by ten. Five per cent: half of ten per cent. One per cent: divide by one hundred. Fifty per cent: halve it. Twenty-five per cent: halve it twice.
scenes.caption: In your head, use building blocks. 10%: divide by 10. 5%: half of 10%. 1%: divide by 100. 50%: halve it. 25%: halve it twice.

scenes.heading: Build it
scenes.question: Find 15% of $350 in your head.
scenes.say: Find fifteen per cent of three hundred and fifty dollars. Ten per cent is thirty-five dollars. Five per cent is half of that: seventeen dollars fifty. Add them: fifty-two dollars and fifty cents.
scenes.caption: Find 15% of $350. 10% is $35. 5% is half of that: $17.50. Add them: $52.50.

scenes.heading: A sale
scenes.question: A $250 bike is 30% off. What is the sale price?
scenes.say: A two hundred and fifty dollar bike is thirty per cent off. The discount is thirty per cent of two hundred and fifty: seventy-five dollars. Take that off: one hundred and seventy-five dollars. Check: you pay seventy per cent, and that's one hundred and seventy-five too.
scenes.caption: A $250 bike is 30% off. The discount is 30% of $250: $75. Take that off: $175. Check: you pay 70%, and 0.7 × 250 = 175 too.

scenes.heading: Watch out

right.title: Wrong
points: Giving the discount as the price

scenes.say: Watch out for these. Don't divide by the percentage: of means multiply. Five per cent is half of ten per cent, not one fifth. And read carefully: is the question asking for the discount or the sale price?

points: Change % to a fraction or decimal
scenes.closing: Ten per cent: divide by ten!
scenes.say: Quick recap. Of means multiply. Change the percentage to a fraction or a decimal. Build mental answers from ten, five and one per cent. Thirty per cent off means you pay seventy per cent. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: Quick recap. "Of" means multiply. Change the percentage to a fraction or a decimal. Build mental answers from 10%, 5% and 1%. 30% off means you pay 70%. Now try the practice questions!
